question: At present, there is growing concern regarding the large-scale dissemination of AI-generated content on TikTok that promotes disinformation narratives undermining the EU and democratic processes. In particular, Polish-language videos generated using artificial intelligence have circulated widely on the platform, calling for Poland’s withdrawal from the EU (‘Polexit’).

The characteristics of this content, including its volume, coordinated distribution patterns, and the use of synthetic voices and personas, suggest the possibility of an organised disinformation campaign. According to Polish authorities, such activity poses a tangible risk to public order, information security and the integrity of democratic debate, not only in Poland, but across the EU. Given this situation: 1.

What supervisory measures does the Commission envisage to ensure that TikTok, as a Very Large Online Platform, fully complies with its obligations under the Digital Services Act1, particularly with regard to systemic risk mitigation and transparency concerning AI-generated content?

Is the Commission considering initiating a formal investigative procedure under the Digital Services Act in order to assess whether TikTok’s current practices adequately address the risks associated with coordinated disinformation campaigns?
OJ L 277, 27.10.2022, pp. 1–102, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/2065/oj.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.2.2026) The Commission is aware of the dissemination of AI-generated content on TikTok advocating for Poland to leave the EU and has, in the framework of the Digital Services Act (DSA)1, engaged in exchanges with the provider of TikTok and third parties regarding the concerned account(s).

The DSA requires providers of very large online platforms (‘VLOPs’), such as TikTok, to assess the risks stemming from their services and to put in place measures to mitigate those risks, including the risks of any actual or foreseeable negative effects on civic discourse and electoral process.

On 17 December 2024, the Commission initiated formal proceedings against TikTok for a suspected breach of the DSA in relation to the obligation to diligently identify, analyse, assess and mitigate systemic risks linked to election integrity, notably in the context of the Romanian Presidential elections on 24 November 20242.

These proceedings focus on the risks linked to the provider’s recommender systems, notably the intentional manipulation or automated exploitation of the service, as well as the provider’s policies on political advertisements and paid-for political content.
The investigations in these proceedings are ongoing, and the Commission continues to gather and analyse evidence and assess any changes made by TikTok to its related systems and processes.

Moreover, the Commission recalls that it has adopted guidelines for VLOPs and very large online search engines (‘VLOSEs’) on the mitigation of systemic risks for electoral processes3, recommending the implementation of efficient and easily recognisable labels on AI-generated content, along with the adoption of robust content moderation processes and algorithmic systems to detect such content.4
